verdict.rationale: Viam publishes its RDK (viam-server) on GitHub and documents running it from source with a local config (`go run ./web/cmd/server -config etc/configs/fake.json`), so the on-machine runtime can run on your own infrastructure. However, the platform's core value is cloud-managed: configuration, fleet management, data sync, ML training, and hosted apps all run on Viam's cloud, and nothing documents a self-hostable control plane. A community member's question about running the server on their own cloud is an open question, not contradicting evidence. Missing for 10: a self-hostable cloud/app control plane (fleet management, data, ML), self-hosting deployment docs, and independent confirmation of running Viam fully without Viam's cloud.
